role: Independent type designer perspective: humanist UI sans construction review; not impersonation or attributed expert opinion
independence: No previous audit, report, or other reviewer output read before writing this report. Font and source unchanged.

findings.condition: UI identifiers, wght100/400/900, 12–16px; verified construction at 48/72px
findings.observation: Capital I has short bars and 1 an angled flag, but lowercase l is a plain stem; O/0 distinction relies chiefly on proportion. At small sizes the diagnostic group needs context, especially in thin weight. This is a limited differentiation vocabulary, not proof that ordinary prose is unreadable.
findings.recommendation: Consider optional hooked l and slashed/dotted zero for identifier-heavy UI; preserve current prose defaults until comparison.
findings.acceptance_test: Blind transcription of randomized I/l/1 and O/0 codes at 12/14/16px, several rasterizers, compare current vs alternate; report error counts before choosing a change.

findings.glyphs: a e s c; RU/EN entire text
findings.observation: Thin strokes render pale and weak beside regular even on black-on-white. Shapes remain coherent at 36–72px. Thin is unsuitable as the default small essential text in this proof.
findings.attribution: intended thin construction interacting with grayscale rasterization; no isolated broken contour demonstrated
findings.recommendation: Keep 100 for sufficiently large display text; select regular for body and essential UI. Do not thicken every master on this evidence.
findings.acceptance_test: At target-device native size, thin labels must meet the same measured transcription accuracy as regular before approving essential small-text usage.

findings.glyphs: e a g; в е ы ь; word spaces
findings.condition: wght900 12–16px, strongest when opsz128 is forced at 14px
findings.observation: Heavy small text has compact counters and a dense texture. At opsz128, spaces and sidebearings visibly contract; RU/EN words in the 14px line approach a continuous dark band. At opsz9 these lines have substantially clearer separation. Large heavy headings remain clear.
findings.attribution: weight and optical-size construction, not a shaping failure; opsz128 at14px is intentionally a mismatch stress test
findings.recommendation: Use matched/automatic optical sizing and avoid heavy for paragraphs. Verify low-opsz counter openness before changing the heavy master.
findings.acceptance_test: Render 900 at 12/14/16px with opsz9/14/16 on CoreText and FreeType; retain discernible counters and word boundaries; compare only matched opsz for product approval.

findings.glyphs: д л м н п и ш щ; a g r n m
findings.observation: Latin double-storey a and single-storey g are familiar; Cyrillic has conventional upright constructions and broadly comparable color. Rectilinear Cyrillic runs produce more repeated verticals than Latin, but no individual malformed letter or strong cross-script size mismatch was evident. Overall character reads closer to a neutral grotesque than a strongly calligraphic humanist sans.
findings.attribution: design character; not a defect by itself
findings.recommendation: Preserve script coherence; if stronger humanist character is a goal, trial localized terminal/shoulder and l differentiation rather than changing Cyrillic to unfamiliar forms.
findings.acceptance_test: Compare mixed-script paragraphs and ш/щ/и/п runs at16px and headings at48px; changes should improve identification without a new script-color imbalance.

limitations: AI visual inspection, not human reading study or an actual named type designer review.
Pillow lacks RAQM; base proof uses BASIC layout. Separate HarfBuzz+FreeType proof checks shaped examples, not the entire corpus.
Only 3 weight instances and sampled optical sizes, not interpolation sweep.
64px long lines clip at right canvas edge; judgments restricted to visible segments; full shorter48px headings are provided in hb-optical-extremes.png.
No exhaustive189-character, kerning-pair, contour topology, or accessibility certification.
